name: Supernumerary Breasts

criteria.description: Presence of additional breast tissue outside the normal pectoral region along the embryonic milk line
Accessory breast tissue located along the embryonic mammary ridge (milk line) extending from axilla to groin
Exclusion of other masses such as lipomas or lymphadenopathy by clinical or imaging evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of accessory breast tissue along the milk line with exclusion of other mass types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging may assist in differentiation from other soft tissue masses

pathognomonic.symptomName: Accessory breast tissue palpable along the milk line
searchTerms: extra breast tissue along chest line

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of nipple-areolar complex within accessory breast tissue

common.symptomName: Tenderness or discomfort in accessory breast tissue during hormonal changes
Visible swelling or enlargement of accessory breast tissue during puberty or pregnancy
Cosmetic concerns related to accessory breast tissue appearance
Occasional lactation from accessory breast tissue during breastfeeding

occasional.symptomName: Infection or inflammation (mastitis) of accessory breast tissue
Development of cysts within accessory breast tissue
Palpable mass or nodularity within accessory breast tissue
Interference with clothing or physical activity due to accessory tissue bulk
searchTerms: extra breast tissue interferes with clothes

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation within accessory breast tissue
rare.notes: Very rare but documented cases of carcinoma

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital anomalies such as renal or skeletal malformations
Psychological distress or body image disorder related to accessory breast tissue

imaging: Ultrasound showing glandular breast tissue in accessory location
MRI for detailed soft tissue characterization if malignancy suspected
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or familial
other: Clinical examination revealing accessory nipple or areola
Histopathology if biopsy performed to exclude malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Soft, mobile fatty mass without nipple or glandular tissue
Associated systemic infection or malignancy signs
Cystic, fluctuant lesions without glandular tissue

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of accessory breast tissue
Ulceration or skin changes over accessory breast tissue
Palpable hard mass within accessory breast tissue
references: Sadove AM, van Aalst JA. Polymastia and polythelia: clinical and histologic study. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1990.
American Journal of Medical Genetics: Congenital anomalies associated with supernumerary breasts
